# Intake Brief: Herdr audit dispatch — deepen per-window batch when the in_review queue is deep (WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS)

## Headline

Make the herdr downtime dispatcher drain a deep `completed`/`in_review` backlog faster by allowing **sequential** audit dispatches to continue within one continuous idle window (up to a small cap) whenever the audit-eligible queue depth reaches `browseItemCount`. Concurrency safety is unchanged: at most one audit is ever active, and every dispatch still passes the idle-duration gate, the ≥2 free-slot minimum, the host-wide audit marker and the per-worklog single-flight.

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher currently requires a fresh full idle period after **every** successful dispatch (`tracker.record(false)` in the worker tick), and the host-wide active-audit marker (WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA) blocks a second audit dispatch while one is running. Under sustained agent traffic, idle windows are rare, so the audit tier drains at roughly one item per idle window even when the `completed`/`in_review` queue is dozens of items deep. The audit skill can already process several items per seeded run (batch drain, SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5), but herdr only ever seeds a single-item `/skill:audit <id>` dispatch.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — wants the review queue to drain during idle compute so items reach release sooner.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deeper than my sprint window, I want the dispatcher to use one idle window for several audits (one after another) instead of one audit per window, so the backlog drains days faster without any extra LLM load.
- **Downtime dispatcher operator** — wants predictable, observable batching that never breaks the safety gates or the host-wide audit slot.
  - *User story:* As an operator, when the queue is shallow I want exactly today's behaviour, and when batching is active I want to see why each extra audit was (or was not) dispatched in the decision log.
- **Audit-tier agents** — must keep receiving one work item per dispatch and never see a duplicate or concurrent audit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Depth-aware batching: an audit-eligible depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` above 1 allows distinct audit continuations inside one idle window until the cap or the depth drop.

  Details: **Depth-aware audit batching (opt-in by depth).** When the audit-eligible backlog — root `completed`/`in_review` items that `classifyItemForDispatch` maps to `audit` (i.e. without a fresh audit and not held) — is at least `browseItemCount`, and `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (default 2, clamped, `1` = legacy/off) is greater than 1, the dispatcher may continue dispatching distinct audit targets within the same continuous idle window until the cap is reached or the depth drops below the threshold. When the depth is below the threshold, behaviour is unchanged: one dispatch per window and a fresh idle period is required before the next.

- Sequential single-audit safety: every continuation re-checks the idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention, code freeze, the active-audit markers and single-flight — no gate is relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset is deferred.

  Details: **Sequential single-audit safety.** The batch continuation never starts a second audit while one is active: it waits for the previous audit's host-wide/per-worklog marker to be released, and re-checks — on every continuation — the continuous idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention (`contention_queue_depth == 0`), the code-freeze marker, the machine-wide active-audit marker and the per-worklog single-flight. No gate is relaxed or bypassed; only the post-dispatch "require a fresh full idle period" reset is deferred for an audit-batch continuation.

- No duplicate or re-dispatched items: each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions, and any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch.

  Details: **No duplicate or re-dispatched items.** Each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions (audit id-guard, staleness-aware marker release, attempt budget, freshness/recency). A failed CAS claim, claim rollback, spawn failure, or any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the current batch rather than skipping to another target.

- Coordination-mode compatibility: the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head without releasing leadership mid-batch, and hands off leadership once at batch end.

  Details: **Coordination-mode compatibility.** On the production coordination path the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head (bounded window extension, same ranking path) without releasing leadership mid-batch; leadership hand-off still occurs once after the batch ends when the fallback was used. When the depth drops below threshold or the cap is reached, normal single-dispatch behaviour resumes immediately.

- Observability: every batch decision is recorded in the downtime decision log with a distinct reason token (`audit-batch-continue` and the existing held/blocked tokens) including depth, cap and remaining; rate limiting is unchanged.

  Details: **Observability.** Every batch decision is recorded in the existing downtime decision log with a distinct reason token (e.g. `audit-batch-continue`, and the existing tokens for held/blocked continuations), including depth, cap and remaining count. Existing reason tokens and rate limiting are unchanged.

- Test coverage in the herdr package: shallow depth keeps the single-dispatch idle reset; depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` yields N sequential audits in one idle window; idle gates, the active-audit marker, the cap, the depth drop and dispatched-marker exclusion are asserted.

  Details: **Test coverage (herdr package).** Unit tests assert: (a) shallow depth keeps today's single-dispatch behaviour including the idle-tracker reset; (b) depth ≥ `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` produces N sequential audit dispatches within one idle window; (c) an unsatisfied idle-duration gate (and sub-2 free slots) blocks all dispatch, including continuations; (d) the host-wide/per-worklog active-audit marker blocks a concurrent continuation, and continuation proceeds only after release; (e) the cap and the depth-drop are respected; (f) dispatched-marker exclusion prevents the same item being selected twice.

- Documentation: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens.

  Details: **Documentation.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

- Full suite: the full project test suite passes with the new changes, at minimum the full herdr package suite.

  Details: **Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (at minimum the full herdr package suite).

## Constraints

- Keep the strict idle-duration gate and `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` for every dispatch: reserve at least one local slot, and never fan out concurrent audits.
- The host-wide single-audit contract (WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA) remains the hard concurrency cap; this item changes only *cadence within one idle window*, never audit concurrency.
- Must not destabilise leader election/lease (5-minute TTL), coordination check-ins, pruning, fail-closed lookups, the review-queue gate, or the coordination offer path.
- Reuse `browseItemCount` (`readReviewQueueGate` / `resolveSprintViewWindow`) as the single "deep queue" threshold; do not add a second depth definition.
- The new setting is `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (settings key `downtimeAuditBatchMax`), default `2`, clamped to a safe range; `1` disables batching and restores legacy behaviour.
- No SorraAgents/audit-skill changes: the audit skill's own batch drain remains the mechanism that processes multiple items after a dispatch; herdr only decides how many audit panes to seed per window.
- Do not change the legacy `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier chain's semantics beyond the shared continuation logic; the production path is coordination mode.
- **Out of scope:** relaxing the host-wide single-audit marker, changing `AUDIT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS`/`AUDIT_BATCH_TIMEOUT` in SorraAgents, and any non-audit batching.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` consumes the Herdr list head and applies safety gates as sequential filters; `dispatchFromCoordination` (leader) dispatches at most one offer per tick and only reads its own extended head as a fallback when nothing in the offer list is dispatchable; the worker `tick()` calls `tracker.record(false)` / `perSlotTracker.record([])` after a successful dispatch, which is the per-window reset.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `readReviewQueueGate` already measures the root-only `completed`/`in_review` count against `browseItemCount` (`resolveSprintViewWindow`), and `classifyItemForDispatch` already decides whether an item is an audit candidate, including freshness/recency.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `getActiveAudit` checks the machine-wide `~/.herdr/downtime/active-audit` marker before the per-worklog dispatch-log marker; `recordDispatch` writes both, `recordPaneClose`/`recordDispatchFailure` release them.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps` wires the Herdr head, `fetchItem`, `getActiveAudit`, dispatch markers and the pane-close hooks.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — downtime settings plumbing, defaults and clamping (the new `downtimeAuditBatchMax` follows the same pattern).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — where the existing single-dispatch and audit-tier behaviour is asserted.

## Desired change

1. Add a bounded, depth-derived batch mode: compute the audit-eligible depth from the already-fetched Herdr head (root `completed`/`in_review` items are mandatory in the head), activate only when `depth >= browseItemCount` and `downtimeAuditBatchMax > 1`, and expose the remaining budget to the dispatch path.
2. In `tick()`, replace the unconditional post-dispatch idle reset with a conditional one: on a successful **audit** dispatch in active batch mode with budget remaining, keep the idle tracker armed for an audit continuation (subject to a fresh per-tick idle/slot/contention re-check); for every other dispatch, or when the budget/threshold no longer applies, preserve today's reset exactly.
3. In `dispatchFromCoordination`, allow the leader to source a continuation audit target from its own head extension after a successful batch-eligible audit dispatch, instead of only after total offer-list exhaustion; defer the own-backlog leadership hand-off until the batch ends.
4. Add `downtimeAuditBatchMax` to settings (default 2, clamped, 1 = off) and thread it through `DowntimeWorkerConfig` and the dispatch options.
5. Record `audit-batch-continue` (and held variants) in the decision log, with depth/cap/remaining metadata, at the existing rate limit.
6. Add the unit tests listed in AC6 and update the dispatcher docs/README.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — batch depth computation, continuation budget, conditional idle reset, leader continuation path, decision-log token.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `downtimeAuditBatchMax` default, parsing and clamping.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — thread the new setting into `createDowntimeWorker`/dispatch config.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` — depth-aware batch activation, cap and marker/single-flight safety tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — shallow-depth regression and idle-reset behaviour.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` — worker-loop continuation, idle gate blocking, leadership hand-off timing.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — leader own-head continuation and distinct-target guarantees.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts` — setting default/clamp coverage.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — activation rule, sequential safety invariants, decision tokens.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — operator-facing description of the new setting.

## Related work

- WL-0MT3PHW4I002SNOV — active-audit single-flight (per-worklog); preserved per item, not relaxed.
- WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA — host-wide audit serialisation; remains the hard concurrency cap.
- WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 — per-tier free-slot minimums (audit needs 2); reused unchanged.
- WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL — downtime dispatcher leader election and coordination.
- WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24 — own-backlog fallback relinquishes leadership; must be deferred to batch end.
- WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9 — sprint-view-only dispatch window (`browseItemCount` head).
- WL-0MT47BQAT00375VB — active-audit detection and audit-tier skip (per-worklog marker).
- WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9 — review-queue depth gate (same `browseItemCount` signal).
- WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD — review-queue gate rewiring (neutral `review-queue-hold`).
- SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5 (SorraAgents) — audit batch drain that consumes the seeded window.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: non-audit tiers could be starved** while a batch continues. Mitigation: batching applies only to audit dispatches and only while `depth >= browseItemCount`; as soon as no audit candidate remains, the normal tier/ranking resumes.
- **Risk: leadership hand-off logic regressed.** The existing own-backlog dispatch releases leadership immediately; deferring it for a batch could strand the leader if the batch never ends. Mitigation: release at batch end, on any failed continuation, and on the next tick when the cap/depth condition no longer holds; cover with an orchestrator test.
- **Risk: the idle-reset change leaks into other kinds.** Mitigation: scope the conditional reset to the audit-batch continuation flag only; add a regression test asserting non-audit dispatch still resets the tracker.
- **Risk: extra `wl` reads per tick hurt latency.** Mitigation: derive depth from the already-fetched head; no new subprocess in the common path.
- **Risk: a continuation starts during a code freeze or after the queue drops.** Mitigation: re-read the freeze marker and re-compute depth on every continuation tick; any frozen/ambiguous state or depth < threshold simply ends the batch and restores normal behaviour.
- **Assumption:** `completed`/`in_review` root items are mandatory-always in the Herdr head, so the head is a complete depth source up to `browseItemCount` and beyond (the existing window extension covers overflow).
- **Assumption:** the host-wide marker is released when the audit pane closes (`recordPaneClose`) or a spawn fails, so a continuation can start promptly without weakening the marker's stale window.
- **Assumption:** a sequential audit batch is acceptable to the audit runner's host-wide `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1` slot because at most one audit pane is active at a time.
- **Scope-creep risk:** relaxing host-wide serialisation (option B) or changing `AUDIT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS` (option C) is explicitly out of scope; if either becomes necessary it should be raised as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (mechanism):** How should "more than one audit per window" work — (A) keep exactly one active audit and continue sequentially within a continuous idle window, (B) dispatch N audit panes in one tick, or (C) seed the audit skill's batch queue with N ids?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(A)** — keep exactly one active audit; when depth ≥ threshold, skip the fresh-idle-period reset so the next audit dispatches once the previous audit pane closes and slots are idle again.
  - **Evidence:** host-wide active-audit marker semantics (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` § Host-wide audit serialisation) and `tick()`'s post-dispatch `tracker.record(false)`.
- **Q2 (threshold):** Reuse `browseItemCount` or add a dedicated threshold?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **Reuse `browseItemCount`** as the single deep-queue signal; add only the small cap `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (default 2).
  - **Evidence:** `readReviewQueueGate`/`resolveSprintViewWindow` already define "deep" for the review-queue gate.
- **Q3 (second target source):** Where should the extra audit target(s) come from in coordination mode?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(A)** the leader re-reads its own Herdr head after the first dispatch (extend the existing own-backlog fallback).
  - **Evidence:** `dispatchFromCoordination`'s own-backlog fallback (`getHerdrListHead` + `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`) and WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7** – RCA: no downtime dispatch overnight despite continuous idle-window status polling (~16 polls/min, 7h idle) (completed)
- **WL-0MSKUG2WI004CBW3** – Check dispatch logs/leases on 192.168.0.191 filesystem (completed)
- **WL-0MRMCO4VB009HIJL** – Tests: getChordByPrefix and arbitrary-depth dispatch (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mt32f90v008uad2, 0mt3phw4i002snov, 60s, ac1 (+120 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mt3phw4i002snov, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+110 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mt32f90v008uad2, 60s, ac1, ac3 (+83 more)

# Documentation: batch setting, activation rule, sequential-safety invariants and decision tokens

Parent AC7: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, its activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens. All related documentation (incl. code comments) is updated and consistent with shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC7: Documentation: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens.

- **Dispatcher doc.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents:
   - the setting (`downtimeAuditBatchMax`, default 2, clamped 1–5, `1` = legacy/off) — in the settings table (~§1638) and the configuration prose;
   - the activation rule (audit-eligible depth ≥ `browseItemCount` from the Herdr head + `auditBatchMax > 1`);
   - the sequential single-audit safety invariants (AC2 gate list — nothing relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset deferred);
   - the new decision tokens (`audit-batch-continue` and held/blocked variants) in the reason-token lists (~§60/108) and observations section;
   - the deferred own-backlog leadership hand-off (WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24 interplay).
- **README.** `packages/herdr/README.md` adds an operator-facing bullet for `downtimeAuditBatchMax` in the settings list (~§521) and notes the batching behaviour (sequentially within one idle window, at most one active audit) in the audit-dispatch section.
- **Code comments.** Comments in `downtime-worker.ts` / `settings.ts` / `index.ts` describing the batch mode, its lifecycle and trade-offs (incl. the proxy-busy caveat: the audit pane's own occupancy still resets the tracker; the deferred reset is only the dispatcher's own post-dispatch reset) match the shipped behaviour in C3–C5.
- **Consistency.** Every documented token, setting name and activation rule matches the implementation; a doc-consistency scan (C7) finds no stale single-dispatch-only claims.

## Minimal Implementation

- Edit the three doc targets and the code comments touched by C3–C5; cross-check reason-token lists, the settings table and the host-wide serialisation section (§1044).
- Verify the AC7 checklist against the shipped behaviour via the verification item (C7).

## Key Files

- docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md
- packages/herdr/README.md
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts (comment blocks)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the implementation items C3, C4, C5 having landed.

## Deliverables

- Updated dispatcher doc, herdr README and code comments, consistent with the shipped behaviour.

# Verification: full suite + documentation consistency (parent AC8)

Final verification slice for WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS. Confirms the full suite passes with the new changes and that all docs are consistent with the shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC6: Test coverage in the herdr package: shallow depth keeps the single-dispatch idle reset; depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` yields N sequential audits in one idle window; idle gates, the active-audit marker, the cap, the depth drop and dispatched-marker exclusion are asserted.
- Covers parent AC8: Full suite: the full project test suite passes with the new changes, at minimum the full herdr package suite.

- **Full suite (AC8).** The full project test suite passes with the new changes — at minimum the full herdr package suite — run via the test skill; a red tree is never pushed (build → test → commit order).
- **Doc consistency (AC7).** A scan of `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference finds no stale references to single-dispatch-only behaviour and no contradiction with the shipped batch mode.
- **AC traceability.** Parent AC1–AC7 each trace to a green spec/behaviour; any gap is recorded in a comment on WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS.
- **Commit hygiene.** The commit message references the parent work item; the changed-scope test gate passes before commit.

## Minimal Implementation

- Run the test skill (full changed-scope suite) once per the shared background-job etiquette; triage any gate-reported failures via the triage skill.
- Cross-check the parent AC list against the spec/test names in `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` and the doc changes.
- Add a completion comment on WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS summarising the verification result and commit hash.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/ (full herdr suite)
- docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md

## Dependencies

- Depends on C1–C6 being committed.

## Deliverables

- Green full suite, doc-consistency sign-off, AC traceability comment on the parent.
